appraisal_events.evidence: Bloch, pas plus que les « gigolos » du monde, ne put prendre part utilement à la discussion... soit par la récente arrivée (de Bloch, par exemple) dans une société différente qu'il abordait de biais, au moment où elle déclinait, dans un crépuscule où le souvenir d'un passé qui ne lui était pas familier ne pouvait l'éclairer.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly marks Bloch as unable to participate meaningfully in the group's shared reminiscence about the dead, because his entry into this society is too recent and oblique for him to share its collective memory.

appraisal_events.evidence: elle restait une Marie-Antoinette au nez autrichien... conservée, embaumée grâce à mille fards... Puis m'ayant quittée, elle se mit à trotter vers la porte... Elle courait, en effet, à son tombeau.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's admiring description of her preserved, 'embalmed' elegance is undercut throughout by mortality imagery and culminates in an explicit narratorial statement that her brisk, sociable exit is in fact a race toward her own death.

status_effects.explanation: Bloch is locally marked as an outsider to the shared generational memory that structures this conversation, excluding him from meaningful participation.

Despite the elaborate praise of her preserved beauty and social vivacity, the narrator's sustained embalming and mortality imagery, capped by the closing line about her running to her tomb, clearly diminishes her within the passage.

ambiguities: The description of princesse de Nassau mixes genuine admiration of her preserved elegance with pervasive mortality/embalming imagery; the passage's dominant movement is read as diminishment because the narrator's closing statement ('elle courait... à son tombeau') explicitly reframes her vivacity as a race toward death, but the surface tone throughout is largely admiring.
